mcqs.q: In FeLV-positive cats at the referral center, the most common associated diagnosis was:
mcqs.e: Neoplasia accounted for 76% of diagnoses, the most common.

mcqs.q: The most common laboratory abnormality in FeLV-positive cats was:
mcqs.e: Anemia occurred in 71%, of which 74% were nonregenerative.

mcqs.q: Regarding age, cats diagnosed with neoplasia were:
mcqs.e: Neoplasia was more likely in younger cats (<4 years).

mcqs.q: Infectious canine distemper virus could be isolated from shelter dogs:
o: Within the first two weeks around peak viral RNA excretion
mcqs.e: Virus isolation succeeded only within the first two weeks, near peak viral RNA (lowest Ct).

mcqs.q: The median duration of a positive RT-PCR result was approximately:
mcqs.e: Median positive-test duration was 34 days, with 25% still positive after 62 days.

mcqs.q: The study proposed which functional marker for the end of infectious risk?
o: Peak viral RNA excretion and the surrounding days
mcqs.e: Peak RNA excretion and days around it correlated with the end of recoverable infectious virus.

mcqs.q: Moxi-doxy is recommended primarily as:
o: An alternative when arsenical treatment is unavailable or inaccessible
mcqs.e: Moxi-doxy is a viable alternative to no treatment when melarsomine cannot be used.

mcqs.q: The most effective non-arsenical regimen described is:
o: Doxycycline 28 days plus monthly topical moxidectin until NAD
mcqs.e: Doxycycline q12-24h for 28 days with monthly moxidectin repeated until no antigen detected.

mcqs.q: Per the review, the safest and most effective heartworm adulticide remains:
mcqs.e: The three-dose melarsomine protocol is still the safest, most effective treatment.

mcqs.q: Post-transport canine parvovirus incidence among the relocated puppies was approximately:
mcqs.e: Incidence of post-transport CPV in 4088 puppies was 2.3%.

mcqs.q: Risk of post-transport CPV was lower in puppies that were:
mcqs.e: Older age (13–17 and 18–19 weeks) and summer transport were associated with lower CPV risk.

mcqs.q: The number and timing of pre-transport vaccinations were:
o: Not associated with post-transport CPV counts
mcqs.e: Vaccine number/timing showed no association; transport timing should weigh other factors.

authors: Isaza D, DiGangi, Isaza N, Isaza R

mcqs.q: Comparing isopropyl alcohol versus water rinse, perioperative rectal temperature:
o: Did not differ significantly between groups
mcqs.e: Mean rectal temperature differences were nonsignificant at every time point.

mcqs.q: The clinical conclusion regarding rinse choice was:
o: Alcohol causes more hypothermia and should be avoided
Either rinse produces the same degree of temperature change
Rinse agent is the main driver of hypothermia
mcqs.e: Both agents gave equivalent temperature change; other hypothermia factors matter more.

mcqs.q: Across both species, the puppies and kittens experienced:
o: Perioperative hypothermia regardless of rinse agent
mcqs.e: Temperatures fell to ~35-36 °C in all groups, reflecting perioperative hypothermia.

mcqs.q: Seroprevalence of Toxoplasma gondii antibodies among the sampled shelter cats was approximately:
mcqs.e: 24 of 84 cats were seropositive (28.6%).

mcqs.q: The definitive host of Toxoplasma gondii is:
mcqs.e: Felids are the definitive host of this zoonotic parasite.

mcqs.q: A key limitation acknowledged by the authors was:
o: Small sample size limiting statistical significance
mcqs.e: The limited sample prevented statistically significant results; framed as a pilot study.

mcqs.q: The two most commonly cited barriers to veterinary care that telehealth aimed to address were:
mcqs.e: Cost and transportation were the cited barriers in underserved communities.

mcqs.q: The proportion of clients reporting they could not have afforded an in-person appointment was:
mcqs.e: 58% said they could not have afforded in-person care; ~25% lacked transportation.

mcqs.q: Client and veterinary student experiences with telehealth were:
mcqs.e: Both client and student experiences were overwhelmingly positive.

mcqs.q: The most common motivations reported by foster caregivers were:
mcqs.e: Most cited animal- or community-based motives, e.g., giving an animal love.

mcqs.q: Compared with females, male caregivers were:
o: Less likely to foster for emotional support
More likely to foster for emotional support
Equally likely to foster for emotional support
mcqs.e: Males had lower odds of fostering for emotional support (OR 0.12).

mcqs.q: Caregivers aged 18–29 were most likely to expect:
o: Companionship, emotional support, and meeting community members
mcqs.e: Young caregivers had higher odds of expecting companionship, emotional support, and social connection.

authors: Powell, Lee, Reinhard, Morris, Satriale, Serpell, Watson

mcqs.q: Compared with non-returning owners, owners who returned their dogs had:
o: Higher expectations for dog behavior/health and the human–dog bond
mcqs.e: Returning owners had significantly higher behavior/health and bond expectations.

mcqs.q: Expectations for ownership responsibilities between returning and non-returning owners:
o: Were the strongest predictor of return
mcqs.e: Ownership-responsibility expectations did not differ between the groups.

mcqs.q: The median length of ownership before dogs were returned was:
mcqs.e: Returns occurred at a median of eight days post-adoption.

authors: Powell, Houlihan, Stone, Gitlin, Ji, Reinhard, Watson

mcqs.q: During COVID-19 (vs the same months of 2019), shelter intake of dogs and cats was:
mcqs.e: Intake of both dogs and cats fell significantly during the pandemic.

mcqs.q: During the pandemic, the overall rate of adoption and euthanasia:
o: Did not differ, though absolute numbers fell with intake
mcqs.e: Rates were unchanged, but absolute adoptions and euthanasias dropped with lower intake.

mcqs.q: The proportion of dogs and cats housed in foster care between 2019 and 2020:
o: Did not significantly differ in the sample
mcqs.e: Despite expansion efforts, the foster-care proportion did not significantly change.

mcqs.q: Factors significantly associated with lower daily weight gain in shelter/foster kittens were:
mcqs.e: Lethargy and female sex were significantly linked to lower daily weight gain.

mcqs.q: Compared with catteries and laboratories, average daily weight gain in shelter/foster kittens was:
o: Higher than reported in those settings
mcqs.e: Despite shelter challenges, average daily weight gain exceeded cattery/lab reports.

mcqs.q: Mortality among the study kittens was approximately:
mcqs.e: Five of 203 kittens (2.5%) died or were euthanized.

journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery Case Reports

mcqs.q: The molecular findings in this shelter FIP outbreak provided support for which theory of pathogenesis?
mcqs.e: Shared and divergent S1/S2 mutations supported a circulating virulent–avirulent theory.

mcqs.q: Diagnosis of FIP in the three cats was confirmed by:
mcqs.e: FIP was confirmed by necropsy, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry.

mcqs.q: The S1/S2 cleavage-site mutation shared by two cats and previously associated with FIP was:
mcqs.e: Two cats shared R790S, a mutation previously linked to FIP development.
